summary: Walkthrough of Aegis Bank's SIG/CAIQ questionnaire and vendor risk concerns. Agreed next steps to share compliance docs and schedule a deeper technical architecture review.

Audit logs, retention, and access controls
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
Encryption at rest/in transit and KMS/HSM details
Vendor risk evidence handoff and timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Samantha Cho: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Samantha from Redwood, AE, and Miguel from our security/infra team is here.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Hi, thanks. We wanted to walk through the SIG — the standard info group questionnaire — and what evidence you can provide for Aegis' vendor risk process.
[00:22] Miguel Alvarez: Great, yeah. We can run through our CAIQ-style answers and point you to artifacts. Quick note up front, some of our doc names and acronyms get transcribed weirdly so I'll try to spell things out.
[00:33] Tom Reynolds: Our procurement timeline is tight, we need SIG back in two weeks ideally.
[00:38] Samantha Cho: Understood. We'll outline what we can share immediately: SOC 2 Type II report redacted, ISO 27001 cert, pen test summary, and a runbook for incident response.
[00:47] Hannah Lee: For technical evidence, we need to see the VPC architecture and how KMS is used — are keys customer-managed? Where are keys stored?
[00:55] Miguel Alvarez: Good question. For our Redwood Private / VPC option keys can be either customer-managed in KMS or we support HSM integrations for enterprise customers. For hosted customers we use envelope encryption and keys are in our cloud KMS, but for Private we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles.
[01:15] Priya Nair: Can you provide proof? Our VRM asks for configuration screenshots and IAM roles and policy docs.
[01:22] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, we can provide architecture diagrams and sanitized policy snippets — not raw secret material. We'll include steps showing role assumption and a sample policy.
[01:33] Tom Reynolds: On audit logs, Aegis requires at least 12 months retention, tamper-evident logs, and S3-style immutable storage options.
[01:42] Samantha Cho: We have configurable retention; by default audit logs are retained for 90 days in hosted, but for enterprise Dedicated/Private we support 12 months or longer and can ship logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[01:55] Miguel Alvarez: Right, and logs can be forwarded via secure syslog or S3 transfer with object lock enabled for immutability. We also have integrity checks — though the paperwork usually shows the hashing pipeline and access controls.
[02:12] Hannah Lee: How about RBAC and SSO? We use Okta and require SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO for role mapping.
[02:20] Miguel Alvarez: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync. RBAC is role-based with fine-grained permissions per route/model. We can map Okta groups to Redwood roles; we also support JIT provisioning.
[02:33] Priya Nair: Does system admins at Redwood have access to customer data?
[02:36] Samantha Cho: Access is scoped. For hosted we do have support/admin roles but access to customer data is logged and limited by RBAC — only a small set of engineers have access under documented processes, and all such access is audited and requires escalation approvals.
[02:50] Miguel Alvarez: Also mention that data access for support is through a bastion workflow and privileged sessions are recorded. We'll include the access control policy and the list of roles with descriptions in the evidence package.
[03:05] Tom Reynolds: Data residency: Aegis requires EU/US separation for certain PII. What regions do you offer?
[03:12] Samantha Cho: We have region pinning for hosted customers across major clouds and for Dedicated we can set capacity in a region. For strict residency we recommend Redwood Private in your VPC or our on-prem package.
[03:24] Hannah Lee: If we go Private, are we still getting your control plane?
[03:28] Miguel Alvarez: For Private deployments we offer a customer-managed control plane; the control plane endpoints can be in your network and we support offline packaging for air-gapped installs if needed.
[03:38] Priya Nair: Encryption at rest/in-transit — what's the algo, and is there BYOK?
[03:42] Miguel Alvarez: TLS 1.2/1.3 for transit, AES-256 for at-rest. BYOK is supported via KMS integration, and we can do envelope encryption with your key material in KMS/HSM. We'll provide a short tech note and config snippets.
[03:59] Samantha Cho: To address the SIG specifically, a lot of the controls map to SOC 2 controls and our documented implementation statements. We can pre-fill CAIQ answers where we have central controls and mark others as "customer responsibility" where integration touches your environment.
[04:15] Tom Reynolds: Are there any red flags we should expect in the SIG?
[04:18] Miguel Alvarez: Sometimes questions around shared responsibility and third-party sub-processors need more detail. We have a sub-processor list and DPIA info. Also questions about continuous penetration testing frequency — we usually provide cadence and scope.
[04:32] Priya Nair: We need sample evidence for encryption key lifecycle and revocation process.
[04:36] Miguel Alvarez: We'll include key rotation schedules and an example of a rotation runbook. For HSM we can show attestation of HSM vendor.
[04:45] Samantha Cho: For the procurement side, Tom, we'll send a single packet with the certificate, SOC report redacted, pen test summary, architecture diagrams, and a pre-filled SIG where possible.
[04:56] Tom Reynolds: That would speed things up. Will you also include SOC 2 coverage dates?
[04:59] Samantha Cho: Yes — reporting period and the auditor name.
[05:03] Hannah Lee: Regarding logging, do you include request-level tracing with model and token metadata? We need to be careful about PII in logs.
[05:12] Miguel Alvarez: We capture request-level metadata for tracing (route, model, latency) but redact PII by default. We also support configurable redaction rules and can avoid persisting full request content if required.
[05:26] Priya Nair: Can you show us the redaction config?
[05:29] Miguel Alvarez: We'll include a sample config and notes on how to enable strict redaction and disable KV cache persistence for sensitive workloads.
[05:41] Samantha Cho: Quick note — some of Redwood's product names get mis-transcribed, for example Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private might show up funny in the SIG; we'll label everything clearly in the packet.
[05:52] Tom Reynolds: On liability and data handling, our legal team wants limited subcontractor access and contractual language — will you sign the standard Addendum?
[06:00] Samantha Cho: We can review with our legal team; Redwood's usual DPA + security addendum covers subcontractor list, data handling, and breach notification SLA. We'll get back with a timeline.
[06:10] Priya Nair: For evidence delivery, can we get S3 access or a secure share with time-limited links?
[06:15] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, we can provide time-limited signed URLs or push artifacts into a pre-provisioned S3 bucket in your account for Private/Dedicated customers.
[06:25] Hannah Lee: About infrastructure: do you use KV cache? Any concerns with cache persistence?
[06:30] Miguel Alvarez: We use KV cache for inference performance; for sensitive tenants we can disable KV caching or ensure it's in-memory and not persisted. We'll document the configuration and options.
[06:45] Samantha Cho: Let's talk timeline: you'll confirm which SIG sections must be fully completed versus "see evidence" and we'll prioritize those.
[06:52] Priya Nair: We'll send a marked-up SIG with required evidence flags by end of day Friday.
[06:56] Miguel Alvarez: Sounds good. We'll aim to get the evidence packet to you by Friday as well: SOC 2, ISO, pen test, architecture diagrams, RBAC/SSO config samples, KMS notes.
[07:08] Tom Reynolds: One thing — do you have any third-party attestations for HSM or key providers?
[07:12] Miguel Alvarez: We'll include vendor attestations where applicable. For cloud KMS providers we rely on their certificates; for HSM appliances we have FIPS/HSM vendor attestations.
[07:23] Samantha Cho: Any other concerns?
[07:25] Priya Nair: Just one: incident notification SLA. We need 72-hour notification for breaches.
[07:30] Samantha Cho: Our standard breach notification is 72 hours; we'll include the incident response timeline and contacts.
[07:36] Hannah Lee: Can we schedule the technical deep dive next week to walk the infra team through the VPC and KMS details?
[07:41] Miguel Alvarez: Yes, I'm available week of 2026-05-04. Let's tentatively schedule and I'll send a calendar invite.
[07:49] Samantha Cho: Great. Recap: Samantha to send compliance packet (SOC 2, ISO, pen test) — due 2026-04-30. Miguel to prepare VPC/KMS diagrams and config snippets and schedule deep dive — due 2026-05-03 for deliverables, deep dive week of 2026-05-04. Priya to confirm SIG evidence list by 2026-04-30.
[08:10] Tom Reynolds: Thanks everyone, that helps.
[08:14] Priya Nair: Thanks, we'll review the packet and follow up with any gaps.
[08:18] Samantha Cho: Thanks all — we'll follow up in writing and attach the artifacts.
[08:22] End of meeting.
